title: WPSS/1874/2005 of SMT.PUSHPA SHARMA Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION NO. 1874 OF 2005 (SS)
Smt. Pushpa Sharma ÖÖ..Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttaranchal and others. ÖRespondents.
Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate for petitioner.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel for State of Uttarakhand.
Ms. Beena Pande, Standing Counsel for State of U.P.
11th November, 2009
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 Heard Mr. D.S. Mehta, Advocate for petitioner, Mr.
N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel for State of Uttarakhandand
Ms. Beena Pande, Standing Counsel for State of U.P.
 This petition was filed by the petitioner praying that
the order dated 22.10.2005 (Annexure -5 to the writ
petition) be quashed. By the said Annexure, the
appointment given to the petitioner under the U.P.
Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants
Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 (from hereinafter
referred to as the Dying in Harness Rules, 1974) was
cancelled. The petitioner, who was the wife of a work-charge employee in Irrigation Department was given
appointment under Dying in Harness Rules vide order
dated 26.7.2004, but subsequently vide order dated
22.10.2005, her services were terminated.
 This Court had granted an interim stay order on
16.12.2005.
 It has been brought to the notice of this Court that
vide stay order, the impugned order has been stayed and

2
the petitioner is still continuing in service. During the
period of pendency of the writ petition, a fresh order has
been passed by the respondents on 10.11.2006 by which
the petitionerís services have been regularised and she
has been absorbed in service as a regular class IV
employee. This fact has been brought by the respondent
by annexing the said order in Supplementary Counter
Affidavit and making averments in the Supplementary
Counter Affidavit.
Learned counsel for the petitioner rightly says that
based on these facts and averments, which have come
from the respondents, he wants to withdraw the writ
petition.
The writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn
accordingly. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
11.11.2009
Rathour
